questions.question: A 42-year-old woman presents with episodic severe headaches, palpitations, and diaphoresis. Her blood pressure in the clinic is 195/110 mmHg. Laboratory evaluation shows markedly elevated 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines. An abdominal MRI reveals a 4 cm mass in the right adrenal gland. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacological intervention prior to surgical resection?

A 54-year-old man presents with progressive bilateral lower extremity edema, fatigue, and frothy urine. Urinalysis reveals 4+ protein and no red blood cells. A 24-hour urine collection quantifies proteinuria at 6.8 g/day. Renal biopsy demonstrates diffuse thickening of the glomerular basement membrane with a 'spike and dome' appearance on silver stain, along with granular deposition of IgG and C3 on immunofluorescence. Autoantibodies against which of the following targets are most commonly associated with this patient's primary condition?
options: Goodpasture antigen (NC1 domain of collagen IV)

questions.question: A 32-year-old woman presents with a 2-month history of nonproductive cough, exertional dyspnea, fatigue, and painful red nodules over her anterior shins. Chest radiography reveals bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and mild reticular opacities. Serum calcium is elevated at 11.2 mg/dL. An elevation in which of the following laboratory markers is most characteristic of this disease process?

A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 5 hours after ingesting a large quantity of acetaminophen in a suicide attempt. Serum acetaminophen concentration measured at 4 hours post-ingestion falls above the treatment line on the Rumack-Matthew nomogram, and intravenous N-acetylcysteine (NAC) therapy is initiated. What is the primary mechanism by which NAC exerts its protective therapeutic effect in this setting?
options: Direct competitive inhibition of cytochrome P450 CYP2E1 activity
Restoration of hepatic glutathione stores to detoxify N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI)
Alkalinization of the urine to promote renal clearance of acetaminophen metabolites
Chelation of acetaminophen in the systemic circulation to form an inactive soluble complex

questions.question: A 40-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with altered mental status, fever, and diffuse petechiae. Peripheral blood smear demonstrates marked schistocytes, and her laboratory results show a platelet count of 11,000/µL, elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and mild serum creatinine elevation. Prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate definitive management?
